newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Beijing slams Manila plan for lighthouse on shoal.
newsitem.headline: Beijing slams Manila plan for lighthouse on shoal.

text.p: China has urged the Philippines to abandon a plan by its military to build a lighthouse on a disputed rock in the South China Sea, Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Sunday.

"They told us, 'please, don't put up a lighthouse there or we will quarrel'," Siazon said in an interview on the private Manila radio station DZRH on the eve of bilateral talks in Beijing between Philipine and Chinese foreign ministry officials.
The Beijing meeting is part of regular talks between the two countries to discuss oustanding issues.
Philippine armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera said earlier this year the military was considering erecting a lighthouse on Scarborough Shoal to assist fishermen.
Manila and Beijing are disputing ownership of the 16-km (10-mile) long rock formation lying about 200 km (125 miles) west of Zambales province on the main Philippine island of Luzon.

China last week invoked 700-year-old documents to assert its claim over the rocks. The Philipines, citing the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea, says it has sovereignty over them because they lie within its exclusive economic zone.
Filipino fishermen last month provoked a Chinese diplomatic protest when they hoisted the Philippine flag over the shoal.
Siazon disputed the Chinese basis of citing history to assert its claim.

"We have said to them that...all claims on territories cannot be based on historical claims ... This is within our exclusive economic zone," he said, adding the shoal had been used for years by Filipino fishermen.
"They said, 'okay, let's talk, but please stop acts of provocation'," Siazon said.

The dispute over Scarborough is separate from the two countries' squabble over the Spratly Islands, a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and atolls which lie well south of the shoal, also in the South China Sea.
Beijing says all islands in the South China Sea historically belongs to China. The Spratlys are also claimed wholly or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
